title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

topics.title: The French Revolution and the idea of the nation

learn.hook: Imagine your whole country deciding: 'We are not the king's subjects any more, we are citizens!' That is what France did in 1789.
points: A nation-state is a state in which most citizens share a sense of common identity and history. Earlier, much of Europe was ruled by dynastic empires that held many different peoples together under one ruling family.
The French Revolution of 1789 transferred sovereignty (supreme power) from the monarch to the body of French citizens.

Revolutionaries spread the ideas of la patrie (the fatherland) and le citoyen (the citizen). The tricolour replaced the royal standard, and the Estates General, elected by active citizens, was renamed the National Assembly.

They set up a centralised administration with uniform laws for all, abolished internal customs duties, brought a uniform system of weights and measures, and made French as spoken and written in Paris the common language.

Napoleon's Civil Code of 1804 (the Napoleonic Code) ended privileges based on birth, made all equal before the law and secured the right to property. But higher taxes, censorship and forced conscription made many conquered people hostile to French rule.

example.q: Think it through: Why would replacing the royal flag with a new tricolour help turn subjects into a nation?
steps: A royal flag stands for one ruling family; the people under it are only subjects.
A tricolour stood for the whole people, not for a king.
When everyone salutes the same new symbol, they feel they belong to one community with shared rights.
So symbols like the flag, new hymns and oaths built a sense of collective identity.
example.answer: The tricolour made people feel that the nation belonged to all citizens, not to the king, which strengthened a shared national identity.

learn.reallife: Our own Tiranga, the national anthem and the Republic Day parade are symbols that make crores of Indians feel they belong to one nation.

games.title: Napoleon's rule: welcomed or resented?

quiz.q: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
quiz.explain: The French Revolution began in 1789. 1815 is the Treaty of Vienna and 1848 is the year of the liberal revolutions.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the French Revolution with later events in Europe

quiz.q: What did the French Revolutionaries mean by 'la patrie'?
quiz.explain: La patrie means the fatherland; le citoyen means the citizen. Both ideas stressed a united community with equal rights.
quiz.mistake: Confuses la patrie with le citoyen

quiz.q: The French Revolution transferred sovereignty from whom to whom?
options: From the church to the king
From the monarch to the body of French citizens
From the citizens to the monarch
quiz.explain: Before 1789 the king held supreme power. The Revolution declared that the people, as citizens, formed the nation and held sovereignty.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the direction of the change

quiz.q: Which language was promoted as the common language of the French nation?
options: French as spoken and written in Paris
quiz.explain: Regional dialects were discouraged and Parisian French became the common language, helping unify the nation.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the revolutionaries encouraged regional dialects

quiz.q: In which year was Napoleon's Civil Code, also called the Napoleonic Code, introduced?
quiz.explain: The Civil Code was introduced in 1804, after Napoleon came to power.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the Code with the start of the Revolution

quiz.q: Which of these did the Civil Code of 1804 do?
options: Gave every adult man and woman the right to vote
Made everyone equal before the law and secured the right to property
Made Latin the language of all courts
quiz.explain: The Code abolished privileges based on birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property.
quiz.mistake: Assumes Napoleon's rule was fully democratic

quiz.q: Why did many people in areas conquered by Napoleon turn against French rule?
options: The French standardised weights and measures
Increased taxation, censorship and forced conscription into French armies
The French improved roads and transport
quiz.explain: The useful reforms were outweighed in people's minds by heavy taxes, censorship and being forced to fight in French armies.
quiz.mistake: Mistakes a popular reform for a cause of hostility

quiz.q: Which statement best describes a nation-state?
options: Each village makes its own laws and coins
A ruling family governs many unrelated peoples by force
Most of its citizens share a sense of common identity and history
quiz.explain: In a nation-state, citizens see themselves as one community. A dynastic empire, by contrast, holds many peoples together under one ruling family.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a nation-state with a dynastic empire

teach.ask: Gappu flaps in: 'Why do people say the French Revolution gave birth to the idea of the nation? Wasn't France already a country?'
teach.praise: Wah! Now I see: France became a nation of citizens, not just a king's land!
teach.nudge: But who held power after 1789, and what symbols did the revolutionaries use to unite people?

topics.title: Liberals, conservatives and the Treaty of Vienna

learn.hook: After Napoleon was defeated, Europe's kings tried to press the rewind button. But new ideas cannot be un-thought!
points: Liberalism comes from the Latin root liber, meaning free. For the new middle classes it meant individual freedom, equality before the law, a constitution, representative government through parliament and the safety of private property.
In revolutionary France, however, the right to vote and to be elected was given only to property-owning men. Women and men without property were left out.
In 1834 a customs union called the Zollverein was formed at the initiative of Prussia. It removed tariff barriers and cut the number of currencies in the German states from over thirty to two.

In 1815 Britain, Russia, Prussia and Austria met at Vienna, hosted by the Austrian Chancellor Duke Metternich. The Treaty of Vienna restored the Bourbon dynasty in France and set up states on France's borders to stop future French expansion.

Conservative regimes used censorship to control newspapers and books. Revolutionaries such as Giuseppe Mazzini, born in Genoa in 1807, formed secret societies: Young Italy in Marseilles and Young Europe in Berne.

example.q: Think it through: Why did German merchants welcome the Zollverein?
steps: Before 1834 goods moving across the German states paid customs duty at many borders.
Each state also had its own currency, weights and measures, so trade was slow and costly.
The Zollverein removed tariff barriers and reduced currencies from over thirty to two.
A single economic territory made trade easier and also strengthened the wish for a united Germany.
example.answer: It removed internal tariffs and cut the number of currencies, making trade cheaper and supporting national unity.

learn.reallife: Just as one GST system replaced many separate state taxes so goods can move more easily across Indian states, the Zollverein made trade simpler across the German states.

games.title: Liberal or conservative idea?
items: Government by consent of the people

quiz.q: The word 'liberalism' comes from the Latin root 'liber'. What does 'liber' mean?
quiz.explain: Liber means free, which is why liberalism stood for individual freedom.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a related idea instead of the actual meaning

quiz.q: What was the Zollverein of 1834?
options: A secret society founded by Mazzini
A customs union formed at the initiative of Prussia
A parliament that met in Frankfurt
A treaty that restored the Bourbons
quiz.explain: The Zollverein was a customs union joined by most German states. It removed tariff barriers between them.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Zollverein with political events of the period

quiz.q: The Zollverein reduced the number of currencies in the German states from over thirty to how many?
quiz.explain: It brought the currencies down from over thirty to just two, making trade far easier.
quiz.mistake: Remembers that currencies were reduced but not by how much

quiz.q: Who hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1815?
quiz.explain: Metternich hosted the Congress, which aimed to undo the changes brought by Napoleon.
quiz.mistake: Picks a famous figure from a different time

quiz.q: Which dynasty did the Treaty of Vienna restore to power in France?
quiz.explain: The Bourbons, who had been removed during the French Revolution, were brought back in 1815.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the ruling family of France with those of Austria, Prussia or Russia

quiz.q: Giuseppe Mazzini founded the secret society Young Italy in which city?
quiz.explain: Young Italy was founded in Marseilles. His other society, Young Europe, was founded in Berne.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Young Italy with Young Europe

quiz.q: Who described Mazzini as 'the most dangerous enemy of our social order'?
quiz.explain: Metternich, the leading conservative of the age, saw Mazzini's revolutionary ideas as a threat to the old order.
quiz.mistake: Assumes someone who worked with Mazzini's cause said it

quiz.q: In revolutionary France, who were given the right to vote and to be elected?
quiz.explain: Liberal ideas of equality did not yet mean universal suffrage: voting was limited to men who owned property.
quiz.mistake: Assumes liberalism meant voting rights for everyone from the start

teach.ask: Gappu tilts his head: 'After Napoleon lost, what did the kings decide at Vienna, and what did liberals want instead?'
teach.praise: Shabash! Kings wanted the old order back, liberals wanted freedom. Tug of war!
teach.nudge: What did the Treaty of Vienna restore, and what freedoms did the liberals ask for?

learn.hook: Metternich once grumbled, 'When France sneezes, the rest of Europe catches cold.' In 1830 and 1848, France sneezed loudly!
points: In July 1830 liberal revolutionaries in France overthrew the Bourbon kings and set up a constitutional monarchy headed by Louis Philippe. This sparked an uprising in Brussels, and Belgium broke away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
The Greek war of independence began in 1821. Supported by many West Europeans, it ended with the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832, which recognised Greece as an independent nation.

Romanticism used art, poetry, music and folk culture to create national feeling. The German philosopher Johann Gottfried Herder said true German culture lived among the common people, das volk. In Poland, under Russian rule, using the Polish language became a sign of resistance.

The 1830s brought hardship: population grew, jobs were few and food prices rose. In 1848 food shortages and unemployment in Paris forced Louis Philippe to flee; a Republic was proclaimed and all adult males above 21 got the vote.

Also in 1848, middle-class liberals in the German states met at the Frankfurt Parliament in the Church of St Paul on 18 May 1848. Its 831 elected representatives offered a crown to Friedrich Wilhelm IV, King of Prussia, but he rejected it. Women could only watch from the visitors' gallery.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the Frankfurt Parliament fail?
steps: It was made up mostly of middle-class professionals and lost the support of workers and artisans.
It offered the crown of a united Germany to Friedrich Wilhelm IV of Prussia.
He rejected it and joined other monarchs opposing the elected assembly.
Without royal or military support and with a narrow social base, the assembly was finally disbanded.
example.answer: It had a narrow middle-class base and was opposed by the monarchy and the army, so it was forced to disband.

learn.reallife: When the Grimm brothers collected German folk tales, they were doing something like collecting dadi-nani stories from Indian villages: saving the voice of ordinary people as part of national culture.

games.title: True or false: 1830 to 1848
items: Belgium broke away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands after the July Revolution of 1830.
The July Revolution sparked an uprising in Brussels that led to Belgium's separation.
Friedrich Wilhelm IV gladly accepted the crown offered by the Frankfurt Parliament.
He rejected the crown and joined other monarchs opposing the assembly.
Herder believed true German culture was found among the common people.
He called them das volk and valued their folk songs, poetry and dances.
Women were full voting members of the Frankfurt Parliament.
Women were admitted only as observers in the visitors' gallery.
In 1848 the French Republic gave the vote to all adult males above 21.
This was a major widening of the right to vote compared to the property-based rules.
Greece became independent through the Treaty of Vienna.
It was the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 that recognised Greece as independent.

quiz.q: Which treaty recognised Greece as an independent nation in 1832?
quiz.explain: The Greek war of independence began in 1821 and the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognised Greece as independent.
quiz.mistake: Confuses this treaty with the better-known Treaty of Vienna

quiz.q: After the July Revolution of 1830 in France, who headed the new constitutional monarchy?
quiz.explain: Liberal revolutionaries overthrew the Bourbon kings and installed a constitutional monarchy with Louis Philippe at its head.
quiz.mistake: Picks another European ruler of the period

quiz.q: How many elected representatives took their places in the Frankfurt Parliament on 18 May 1848?
quiz.explain: 831 elected representatives marched to the Church of St Paul in Frankfurt.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the number with the year or the 39 German states

quiz.q: To whom did the Frankfurt Parliament offer the crown of a united Germany?
options: Friedrich Wilhelm IV, King of Prussia
quiz.explain: The crown was offered to Friedrich Wilhelm IV, who rejected it. William I later became German Emperor in 1871.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Friedrich Wilhelm IV with William I

quiz.q: According to Johann Gottfried Herder, where was true German culture to be found?
options: In the decisions of the Congress of Vienna
quiz.explain: Herder believed folk songs, folk poetry and folk dances of ordinary people expressed the true spirit of the nation.
quiz.mistake: Assumes culture belongs only to the elite

quiz.q: Why did speaking Polish become a symbol of struggle in the 19th century?
options: Polish was banned by Napoleon's Civil Code
Poland was under Russian rule and Russian was imposed, so using Polish showed resistance
Polish was the language of the Frankfurt Parliament
Polish was the official language of the Russian Tsar
quiz.explain: Under Russian rule, Polish was forced out of schools and Russian was imposed everywhere, and an armed rebellion in 1831 was crushed. Using Polish for church gatherings and religious teaching became a symbol of the struggle against Russian dominance.
quiz.mistake: Does not link language to resistance against foreign rule

quiz.q: When the Republic was proclaimed in France in 1848, the vote was given to all adult males above what age?
quiz.explain: The National Assembly granted suffrage to all adult males above 21 and guaranteed the right to work.
quiz.mistake: Uses today's voting age of 18 instead of the historical figure

quiz.q: What role were women allowed at the Frankfurt Parliament?
options: They were elected as half the members
Only observers in the visitors' gallery
quiz.explain: Though many women had taken part in the liberal movement, they were denied the right to vote and sat only in the visitors' gallery.
quiz.mistake: Assumes liberals of 1848 supported equal political rights for women

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'Why is 1848 called a year of revolutions? Did anything actually change?'
teach.praise: Superb! Liberals rose up in 1848, but kings and armies pushed back. Got it!
teach.nudge: What happened at the Frankfurt Parliament, and who refused its crown?

learn.hook: Two puzzles, two master builders: Bismarck fitted Germany together with 'blood and iron', while Cavour and Garibaldi assembled Italy piece by piece.
points: After 1848, nationalism moved away from democratic revolution. Conservatives used state power and armies to build nations.

Prussia led German unification. Its chief minister Otto von Bismarck, backed by the Prussian army and bureaucracy, fought three wars over seven years, with Austria, Denmark and France, all won by Prussia.

In January 1871 the Prussian king, William I, was proclaimed German Emperor in a ceremony at the Hall of Mirrors in Versailles. The new state focused on modernising currency, banking, and the legal and judicial systems.

In the mid-19th century Italy was divided into seven states. Only Sardinia-Piedmont was ruled by an Italian princely house; the north was under the Austrian Habsburgs, the centre under the Pope and the south under the Bourbon kings of Spain.

King Victor Emmanuel II and his chief minister Count Cavour led unification. Through a diplomatic alliance with France, Sardinia-Piedmont defeated Austria in 1859. In 1860 Giuseppe Garibaldi's volunteers marched into the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, and in 1861 Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of united Italy.

example.q: Think it through: Mazzini's uprisings of 1831 and 1848 failed. Why did Sardinia-Piedmont succeed later?
steps: Mazzini relied on secret societies and revolutionary uprisings without a strong state behind them.
Sardinia-Piedmont was a kingdom with its own army and a skilled chief minister, Cavour.
Cavour made a diplomatic alliance with France, which helped defeat Austria in 1859.
Garibaldi's volunteers then won the south, and the movement came together under King Victor Emmanuel II in 1861.
example.answer: Unification succeeded when a strong state with an army and clever diplomacy took the lead, joined by popular volunteers.

learn.reallife: Just as hundreds of princely states had to be brought together into the Indian Union after 1947, Germany and Italy had to join many separate states into one country.

games.title: Germany or Italy?
items: William I proclaimed Emperor at Versailles
Wars with Denmark, Austria and France

items.text: German unification was led by the state of ___.
In 1871 William I was proclaimed German Emperor at ___.
The chief minister of Sardinia-Piedmont was Count ___.
In 1861 ___ was proclaimed king of united Italy.

quiz.q: Who was the chief minister of Prussia who led the unification of Germany?
quiz.explain: Bismarck, with the Prussian army and bureaucracy, was the architect of German unification.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the German and Italian leaders

quiz.q: Who was proclaimed German Emperor in January 1871?
quiz.explain: The Prussian king William I became German Emperor. Bismarck was his chief minister, not the emperor.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Bismarck himself became emperor, or confuses William I with Friedrich Wilhelm IV

quiz.q: Where was the new German Empire proclaimed in 1871?
options: In the Church of St Paul, Frankfurt
In the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
quiz.explain: The ceremony took place at the Palace of Versailles in France, after Prussia's victory over France.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the Frankfurt Parliament of 1848

quiz.q: Prussia fought three wars over seven years to unify Germany. Against which countries?
quiz.explain: Prussia defeated Austria, Denmark and France, and these victories completed unification.
quiz.mistake: Guesses large powers at random

quiz.q: Before unification, which was the only Italian state ruled by an Italian princely house?
options: The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
quiz.explain: The north was under Austria, the centre under the Pope and the south under the Bourbon kings of Spain; only Sardinia-Piedmont had an Italian ruling house.
quiz.mistake: Does not know who ruled each part of Italy

quiz.q: How did Cavour help bring about Italian unification?
options: He led armed volunteers into the south of Italy
He made a diplomatic alliance with France that helped defeat Austria in 1859
He founded the secret society Young Italy
He was crowned king of Italy in 1861
quiz.explain: Cavour was neither a revolutionary nor a democrat; he used diplomacy. Garibaldi led the volunteers, Mazzini founded Young Italy and Victor Emmanuel II became king.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of the leaders of Italian unification

quiz.q: In 1860, Garibaldi's armed volunteers marched into which region?
options: South Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
quiz.explain: Garibaldi won the support of local peasants and drove out the Spanish Bourbon rulers from the south.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the geography of Italian unification

quiz.q: In which year was Victor Emmanuel II proclaimed king of united Italy?
quiz.explain: 1859 was the defeat of Austria, 1860 Garibaldi's march, and 1861 the proclamation of Victor Emmanuel II as king.
quiz.mistake: Confuses this with the defeat of Austria (1859) or German unification (1871)

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: 'Who put Germany and Italy together, and how did they do it?'
teach.praise: Wonderful! Bismarck for Germany, Cavour and Garibaldi for Italy. My feathers are standing up!
teach.nudge: Which state led each unification, and who were the key leaders?
